title.narrative: Strengthening African Civil Society and Governments’ leadership and voices on Climate Change

description.narrative: The decisions agreed at COP 26 made progress towards addressing the climate crisis but fell short of key expectations and asks of the vulnerable countries, including the Africa Group. The COP failed to raise the twice-promised $100bn annual climate funding to vulnerable countries, did not close the mitigation and adaptation ambition gaps in line with staying below 1.5°C. At COP29 country parties failed to agree to scale up climate finance to the requisite US$1,3trillion via the new collective quantified goal (NCQG) leaving climate-affected countries to the vices of climate catastrophe's and debt as a result of limited capacity to raise climate finance.. The science and message from leaders from vulnerable developing nations and organisations is unequivocal; failure to effectively implement the Paris Agreement and close the mitigation, adaptation, and financial gaps in this decade will mean that the opportunity to make the world safe for the present and future generations will be lost. COP27, 28 and 29 held in Egypt, UAE and Azerbaijan respectively, provided opportunities for the continent to ensure that fair and ambitious outcomes that meet the needs of climate vulnerable countries and communities are met. Africa remains the most vulnerable continent severely affected by climate change. International climate policy and processes including mobilisation around COPs present opportunities to catalyse green and resilient investments in the continent. Despite the challenges and opportunities presented by climate change, Africa is the least engaged region on climate diplomacy and there is currently minimal public debate on clean energy and climate change. This is because there are structural barriers, including capacity gaps both within national and regional African decision-making bodies, as well as within civil society and other non-state actors that could otherwise support enhanced climate leadership. Power Shift Africa will help facilitate informed and effective participation of Africa in the global climate change negotiations including at the UNFCCC through building capacities of government officials and CSOs, support effective media campaign and promoting ambitious and equitable positions and demands, and helping to secure a fair, robust and science-based outcomes at COP30.
